profile.reading:
This building is SLC4, one of five data centers DataBank operates on its Granite Point Campus in Bluffdale, Utah, roughly 20 miles south of Salt Lake City. DataBank's own campus page places SLC4 at 14860 S Pony Express Road, Bluffdale, UT 84065, with 20,740 square feet of IT space and 3.67 megawatts of critical IT load. A third-party aggregator lists this facility under the neighboring city of Riverton, Utah and states 2.0 megawatts of power, both figures that conflict with DataBank's own page; DataBank's own materials, which consistently place all five buildings in Bluffdale, are treated as authoritative here. DataBank acquired the underlying Granite Point site from C7 Data Centers in 2017. Across the full five-building campus, DataBank states a combined 257,770 square feet of IT space and roughly 45.9 megawatts of critical IT load on about 23 acres, fed by diverse A and B power feeds from Rocky Mountain Power in an N+1 substation configuration, with FISMA, SSAE 18, HIPAA/HITECH, PCI, and ISO 27001 compliance certifications applicable campus-wide. DataBank does not publish a specific year-opened date for SLC4 on its current site. Utah's "Silicon Slopes" technology corridor has grown substantially around Salt Lake and Utah counties over the past decade, drawing data center, software, and financial-technology employers, and Bluffdale's industrial-zoned land along the Pony Express Road corridor has become a recognized data center cluster anchored by DataBank's campus alongside other operators in the immediate area.

Rocky Mountain Power filed for what it described as Utah's first major large-load energy agreement under the state's 2025 large-load legislation in early February 2026, an "Operation Gigawatt" filing with the Utah Public Service Commission covering a data center customer that agreed to cover its own service costs; this filing does not name DataBank or the Granite Point campus specifically, so it is noted here only as regional grid-planning context, not as a confirmed connection to SLC4. Utah's broader "Silicon Slopes" branding effort has helped position the state as a lower-cost alternative to coastal data center markets for operators seeking reliable power and a business-friendly regulatory climate.

[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed in the registry to DataBank. DataBank Ltd. was established in 2005 in a historic former Federal Reserve Bank building in downtown Dallas, Texas, that had been converted to a data center in 1999, per DataBank own corporate history page fetched this session. DataBank was acquired in July 2016 by a group of investors led by DigitalBridge, per that same page. DataBank own history page also lists a series of acquisitions expanding its footprint, three Salt Lake City area data centers from C7 Data Centers plus facilities in Cleveland and Pittsburgh from 365 Data Centers in January 2017, Lightbound, an Indianapolis based provider, in December 2018, United States and United Kingdom data center assets from zColo in December 2020, and four Houston area data centers from CyrusOne for 670 million dollars in January 2022. A trade press article fetched this session, from pe-insights.com, reports that DigitalBridge agreed to sell a 27 percent fully diluted equity stake in DataBank to Swiss Life Asset Management and EDF Invest for about 1.2 billion dollars, expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2022, reducing DigitalBridge own stake to about 15.5 percent and yielding DigitalBridge about 230 million dollars in cash proceeds. DataBank own history page states the company now operates more than 65 data centers across more than 27 markets. The operator own dedicated page for this facility, Granite Point Campus SLC4, fetched this session, confirms the address already on file, 14860 S Pony Express Rd, Bluffdale, UT 84065, and states 3.67 MW of critical IT load and 20,740 IT square feet.

reading.body:
DataBank SLC4 publishes 3.67 MW of IT capacity across 20,740 square feet, making it a boutique facility rather than hyperscale. At common AI training density, this capacity supports roughly 92 racks, which sets a hard ceiling on what any tenant can deploy there.

The operator describes the site as equipped with a private power substation and positioned for high-density, compute-intensive workloads. This configuration matches what AI inference and HPC jobs require, but the published megawatt figure is the binding constraint. The facility is one of three on the Granite Point Campus, meaning tenants could theoretically access more power across the wider site, but SLC4 itself cannot exceed what is published.

Among Utah facilities with disclosed capacity, SLC4 ranks fourth out of 51.69 MW total, representing about 7 percent of that published pool. Twenty-one facilities are mapped in the state, but most publish no capacity figure, so the true inventory is larger and the ranking reflects only the disclosed subset. For an AI buyer, the honest value is narrow: a small, dense colocation option in a mid-tier market with existing substation infrastructure, suited to a tenant needing focused compute density rather than scale.
